editorial:
If you love dark crime stories set in snowy landscapes, this one pulls you in fast. Detective Harry Hole is a troubled but brilliant investigator who gets pulled into a chilling case when a woman vanishes and her pink scarf turns up wrapped around a creepy snowman. The cold Norwegian setting gives everything a moody, tense feel, and the mystery keeps you guessing about who is behind the killings. It is the kind of movie that makes you want to grab a blanket and watch with the lights off.

The acting is solid, especially from the lead, and the snowy visuals look great in high definition. On the downside, the story can feel confusing at times, and some plot threads do not fully pay off. Still, if you enjoy slow-burn thrillers with a dark edge, you will find plenty to like here. It is best enjoyed streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, renting on Apple TV, or picking up the 4K Blu-ray for the sharpest picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Harry Hole tracks down the killer, who has been targeting women connected to a past case. The twist reveals the snowman builder's identity and motive tied to a personal grudge. Harry confronts him in a tense showdown, and the killer is stopped before claiming another victim. The movie ends with Harry reflecting on the case, leaving you with a dark but satisfying close to the mystery.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark crime thrillers and snowy mysteries.
